text:
Jess: heads-up — a bunch of customers are seeing 502/504s on hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. Main hits: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. customer examples coming in.
monitoring-bot: ALERT high error rate: redis-prefix-cache-prod error rate 18% p95 latency 2.1s, fired at 2026-03-15T09:13:05Z
Jess: attaching a snippet from our API gateway: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:58Z] upstream timed out (110) "GET /v1/generate" service=api-gateway code=504
[2026-03-15T09:12:59Z] backend error "GET /v1/chat" err="redis: client is closed" status=502
```
Tom: ok i'm looking at the cache tier. Running `redis-cli -h cache-01 info` shows blocked_clients = 95 and used_memory_rss spikes. Also seeing NOAUTH on a subset of hosts.
Ryan: I see the same on memcached pool: `STAT curr_connections 1024` and repeated "connection reset by peer". Looks like connection pools exhausted.
Sophia: any config changes rolled to caching cluster recently?
deploy-bot: config-change:cache-credentials rotated by infra/ryan at 2026-03-15T09:09:12Z — rollout target: redis-prefix-cache-prod (canary -> all)
Ryan: that was me, we rotated read-only credentials to expire an old key. Can confirm one of the redis nodes didn't get the new cred (edge case with the canary script). Some clients are getting WRONGPASS/NOAUTH and are retrying/slowdown which blows up p99 latency and pool limits.
Jess: repro steps for support/investigation:
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <valid-key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
2) watch gateway logs for 502/504
3) check redis: `redis-cli -h cache-01 -a <rotated-pass> ping` (some nodes respond PONG, others NOAUTH)

Example error we captured from an agent: `ERR Client sent AUTH, but no password is set` and also `ERR wrong number of arguments for 'auth' command` — looks like credential mismatch + client library retries.
Tom: immediate mitigation options:
- fail-open on cache reads so API can hit model serving directly (short-term, increases cost)
- set circuit-breaker to 30% error and short-circuit caches
- roll back credential rotation to previous working secret (if that's fast)

Sophia: do the fail-open now. I'll patch API config to set CACHE_BYPASS=true for hosted api-prod route and restart pods (kubectl rollout restart). This will short-circuit the prefix cache, avoid KV ops blocking handlers.
Ryan: i'm also killing the stale client processes on the 3 nodes that didn't pick up creds, and reapplying the new secret rollout with strict ordering.
Lee: I'll message affected customers and open a ticket with critical label. Draft msg: "We're investigating increased timeouts/5xx for inference; we're bypassing cache to restore service, will follow up with root cause and ETA." :loudspeaker:
Jess: steps executed:
- 09:20 UTC set CACHE_BYPASS=true for api-prod via service-config, restarted gateway: `kubectl -n platform set env deployment/api-gateway CACHE_BYPASS=true` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/api-gateway`
- 09:22 UTC ran `redis-cli -h cache-02 acl setuser default on >password` on affected nodes to sync creds (manual interim)
- 09:23 UTC restarted memcached pool members behind pool-3 (graceful)

After bypass: error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.4% within 3 minutes. p95 latency improved but token costs will increase while bypass is on.
Tom: logging note — capture full redis auth failures and client stack traces (client-id headers) for postmortem. Also add a guard in the rotation script to fail if any node reports NOAUTH.
Ryan: next steps on infra: re-run rolling credential update with canary verification: check `redis-cli -h $host ACL WHOAMI` and `CLIENT LIST` to ensure no stale clients, then proceed. Also bump connection pool size temporarily.
Sophia: product note — revisit cache fallback strategy: prefer degrade to cached stale values before full bypass to lower model load.
Lee: tickets created: SUPPORT-4921 (customer comms), SRE-2108 (postmortem + runbook update), INFRA-883 (credential rotation guard).
Jess: closing this thread for now — service restored via cache bypass and node fixes. Please add any missing follow-ups here. Will move to postmortem doc with timeline + remediation. :white_check_mark:
